title: Distinguishing a Random Permutation Square
summary: To the proposers' best knowledge, it is unexplored how many queries are needed to distinguish the square of a uniformly random permutation from a uniformly random permutation.

formal_statement.body: Determine how many queries are needed to distinguish the squared permutation $P \circ P$, where $P$ is a uniformly random permutation, from a uniformly random permutation $E$. This simple-to-state problem is, to its proposers' best knowledge, unexplored.

scope.domain: Query complexity for distinguishing distributions over random permutations and their squares.
assumptions: P is a uniformly random permutation.
E is a uniformly random permutation.
parameters: Number of queries, measuring the cost of distinguishing the two permutation distributions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the query complexity of distinguishing the square of P from E.

progress.summary: The source presents this as a simple-to-state problem related to the permutation counting needed for the single-permutation security proof. It states that, to the proposers' best knowledge, the problem is unexplored.
citation_labels: Shan Chen et al., Minimizing the Two-Round Even-Mansour Cipher
